item.title: Indigenous consultation key to 'new' Champlain Monument redesign
item.description: Signature Memorials of Orillia is 'advancing conceptual design options for how the statuary may be reimagined within the park' next year, say officials

item.title: Bus carrying junior hockey team crashes in northern Alberta, two sent to hospital
item.description: ATHABASCA — Mounties in northern Alberta say there were multiple injuries after a bus carrying a junior hockey team went off a slippery and snow-covered highway.

item.title: Man pleads guilty to impaired, failure to remain in 2023 crash where he tried to outrun police
item.description: Arlow Buehler has admitted guilt to charges stemming from a south-end Barrie collision and attempted escape while intoxicated; he will be sentenced in February

item.title: VIDEO: These digital billboards are watching you right back
item.description: Tonight on 'Closer Look': The federal Privacy Commissioner is investigating the use of anonymous video analytics (AVA), a controversial ad technology that tracks the age and gender of people walking by

item.title: Lost for decades, war medals returned to Barrie senior
item.description: 'I just cried,' said Barrie senior Marie Warren, who was recently presented with replacement war medals more than 80 years after misplacing them following her service in the Second World War

item.title: Poilievre says Carney trying to manipulate his way to majority with floor-crossings
item.description: OTTAWA — Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is accusing Prime Minister Mark Carney of trying to "wheel and deal" his way to a majority government after a second Tory MP joined the Liberal caucus.

item.title: Libraries say budget proposal to end shipping program would be 'catastrophic'
item.description: ST. JOHN'S — Libraries across Canada say a proposed change in the federal budget bill would end their ability to ship books at reduced rates, threatening interlibrary loan programs and possibly forcing the closure of rural facilities.

item.title: Lawyer says B.C. Mountie should be fired immediately or quit over group-chat remarks
item.description: A Mountie accused of making racist and sexist comments in group chats should be dismissed immediately or directed to resign within 14 days, the lawyer for the RCMP's conduct authority told an adjudication board hearing Friday.

item.title: Eby plans $150 million in loan guarantees for Cowichan land owners

item.title: Abbotsford mayor blasts feds for flooding 'inaction' as water starts receding
item.description: ABBOTSFORD — The mayor of flood-struck Abbotsford, B.C., says he is disappointed and frustrated with the federal government over what he calls "inaction" on cross-border flooding that has repeatedly inundated his city.
